claim: Multiple, functionally specialized cohesin complexes mediate the establishment and two-step release of sister chromatid cohesion in C. elegans meiosis.
source: We show that multiple, functionally specialized cohesin complexes mediate the establishment and two-step release of sister chromatid cohesion that underlies the production of haploid gametes.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including immunofluorescence, genetic analysis, and sister chromatid cohesion assays.

claim: The kleisin subunits REC-8 and COH-3/4 differ between meiotic cohesins and endow them with distinctive properties.
source: In C. elegans, the kleisin subunits REC-8 and COH-3/4 differ between meiotic cohesins and endow them with distinctive properties that specify how cohesins load onto chromosomes and then trigger and release cohesion.
evidence: Supported by data showing differential loading mechanisms (Figure 2), different timing of accumulation (Figure 1E), and distinct removal patterns (Figure 6B).

claim: COH-3/4 cohesin becomes cohesive through a replication-independent mechanism initiated by DNA double-stranded breaks.
source: Unlike REC-8 cohesin, COH-3/4 cohesin becomes cohesive through a replication-independent mechanism initiated by the DNA double-stranded breaks that induce crossover recombination.
evidence: Supported by data showing COH-3/4 accumulates after premeiotic S phase (Figure 1E), requires SPO-11-dependent DSBs for sister chromatid cohesion (Figure 3E), and can be restored by γ-irradiation in spo-11 mutants (Figure 3E).

claim: Break-induced cohesion tethers replicated meiotic chromosomes.
source: Thus, break-induced cohesion also tethers replicated meiotic chromosomes.
evidence: This is an inference from the finding that COH-3/4 cohesin establishes cohesion in response to DSBs after DNA replication is complete.

claim: Recombination stimulates separase-independent removal of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins from reciprocal chromosomal territories flanking the crossover site.
source: Later, recombination stimulates separase-independent removal of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins from reciprocal chromosomal territories flanking the crossover site.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing complementary patterns of REC-8 and COH-3/4 on bivalents (Figure 6B), persistence of this pattern in sep-1 mutants (Figure 7B), and absence of differential removal in spo-11 mutants (Figure 7A).

claim: Region-specific removal of cohesins likely underlies the two-step separation of homologs and sisters.
source: This region-specific removal likely underlies the two-step separation of homologs and sisters.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that COH-3/4 is enriched at short arms where SCC is released at anaphase I, while REC-8 is enriched at long arms where SCC persists until anaphase II, combined with prior knowledge of rec-8 and coh-3/4 mutant phenotypes.

claim: COH-3/4 performs cohesion-independent functions in synaptonemal complex assembly.
source: Unexpectedly, COH-3/4 performs cohesion-independent functions in synaptonemal complex assembly.
evidence: Supported by data showing robust SC assembly in spo-11 rec-8 mutants that have COH-3/4 binding but lack COH-3/4-mediated cohesion, while SC assembly fails in rec-8; coh-4 coh-3 mutants that lack COH-3/4 binding (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Approximately 30% of human zygotes have abnormal chromosomal content at conception due to defects in meiosis.
source: Approximately 30% of human zygotes have abnormal chromosomal content at conception due to defects in meiosis.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Hassold and Hunt, 2001) as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Aneuploidy is a leading cause of miscarriages and birth defects.
source: Such aneuploidy is a leading cause of miscarriages and birth defects (Hassold and Hunt, 2001), and is thought to result, in part, from defects in sister chromatid cohesion (SCC) (Chiang et al., 2012; Jessberger, 2012; Nagaoka et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion is critical for accurate chromosome segregation.
source: SCC tethers replicated sister chromatids during mitosis and meiosis and is critical for accurate chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of cell biology.

claim: The cohesin complex is composed of Smc1, Smc3, Scc3, and an α-kleisin subunit.
source: The cohesin complex is composed of two long coiled-coil proteins of the Structural Maintenance of Chromosomes (SMC) family, called Smc1 and Smc3, a non-SMC protein called Scc3, and a fourth subunit called the α-kleisin (Nasmyth and Haering, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, cited from prior literature.

claim: Smc1, Smc3 and the kleisin form a tripartite ring proposed to mediate sister chromatid cohesion by encircling sister chromatids.
source: Smc1, Smc3 and the kleisin form a tripartite ring proposed to mediate SCC by encircling sister chromatids.
evidence: This is a widely accepted model in the field, based on prior research.

claim: During yeast meiosis, the mitotic kleisin Scc1 is replaced by the meiosis-specific kleisin Rec8.
source: During yeast meiosis, the mitotic kleisin Scc1 is replaced by the meiosis-specific kleisin Rec8 (Klein et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Klein et al., 1999.

claim: Rec8 is not the sole meiotic kleisin in many organisms.
source: We recently showed that the dual kleisin model derived for yeast is insufficient to explain how cohesin complexes facilitate the reduction of genome copy number in all organisms, since Rec8 is not the sole meiotic kleisin in many organisms (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009) and is supported by the discovery of COH-3/4 in C. elegans and similar kleisins in plants and mammals.

claim: Rec8 cohesin is essential for crossover recombination formation and maintenance.
source: COs promote accurate homolog segregation during anaphase of meiosis I, and Rec8 cohesin is required for efficient CO formation and maintenance.
evidence: This is established from analysis of rec8 mutants in numerous organisms, as cited in the text (DeVeaux and Smith, 1994; Bhatt et al., 1999; Klein et al., 1999; Watanabe and Nurse, 1999; Buonomo et al., 2000; Pasierbek et al., 2001; Yokobayashi et al., 2003; Bannister et al., 2004; Parra et al., 2004; Chelysheva et al., 2005; Severson et al., 2009; Tachibana-Konwalski et al., 2010; Shao et al., 2011).

claim: Rec8 cohesin facilitates co-orientation of sister chromatids in meiosis I.
source: Rec8 cohesin facilitates co-orientation.
evidence: This is established from analysis of rec8 mutants in numerous organisms, as cited in the text.

claim: Rec8 cohesin is essential for the linkages that tether sisters until anaphase II.
source: Rec8 cohesin is essential for the linkages that tether sisters until anaphase II.
evidence: This is established from analysis of rec8 mutants in numerous organisms, as cited in the text.

claim: C. elegans gametogenesis requires COH-3 and COH-4 in addition to REC-8.
source: Our recent work challenged this prevalent view by demonstrating that Caenorhabditis elegans gametogenesis requires two nearly identical and functionally redundant predicted α-kleisins, called COH-3 and COH-4 (hereafter, COH-3/4), in addition to REC-8 (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: REC-8 and COH-3/4 together mediate meiotic sister chromatid cohesion.
source: REC-8 and COH-3/4 together mediate meiotic SCC, and severe disruption of SCC occurs only when all three kleisins are removed, suggesting the formation of cohesin complexes that differ in their kleisin subunit.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009) and supported by data in Figure 3D showing sister separation in kleisin triple mutants.

claim: REC-8 and COH-3/4 are required for crossover recombination.
source: Moreover, REC-8 and COH-3/4 are required for CO recombination.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: Crossover recombination fails in rec-8 single mutants and in coh-4 coh-3 double mutants.
source: CO recombination fails in rec-8 single mutants and in coh-4 coh-3 double mutants, causing homologs to remain detached.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: COH-3/4 cannot co-orient sisters or mediate sister chromatid cohesion that persists until anaphase II.
source: Unlike REC-8, COH-3/4 cannot co-orient sisters or mediate SCC that persists until anaphase II.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009) and is based on the phenotype of rec-8 mutants where sisters separate at anaphase I.

claim: In rec-8 mutants, sister chromatids are tethered by COH-3/4-dependent sister chromatid cohesion until anaphase I, when they segregate prematurely toward opposite spindle poles.
source: Consequently, in rec-8 mutants, sister chromatids are tethered by COH-3/4-dependent SCC until anaphase I, when they segregate prematurely toward opposite spindle poles (equational division).
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: In coh-4 coh-3 mutants, REC-8 cohesin co-orients sisters during meiosis I and tethers sisters until anaphase II.
source: In contrast, in coh-4 coh-3 mutants, REC-8 cohesin co-orients sisters during meiosis I and tethers sisters until anaphase II.
evidence: This is cited from the authors' prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: Meiotic kleisins similar to COH-3/4 have been identified in plants and mammals.
source: Subsequent to the discovery of COH-3/4 in C. elegans, meiotic kleisins similar to COH-3/4 were identified in plants and mammals (Herran et al., 2011; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011; Llano et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature showing the discovery of similar kleisins in other organisms.

claim: Cohesion persists in rec8 mutants of Arabidopsis, maize, mouse, and C. elegans.
source: The involvement of these kleisins in meiotic SCC likely explains why cohesion persists in rec8 mutants of Arabidopsis, maize, and mouse, as it does in C. elegans (Bhatt et al., 1999; Bannister et al., 2004; Chelysheva et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2005; Golubovskaya et al., 2006; Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature and the authors' prior work.

claim: REC-8 and COH-3/4 co-localized with the chromosomal axis protein HTP-3 in pachytene nuclei of wild-type animals.
source: Indeed, REC-8 and COH-3/4 co-localized with the chromosomal axis protein HTP-3 (Goodyer et al., 2008) in pachytene nuclei of wild-type animals (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The COH-3/4 antibody recognizes COH-3 and COH-4 specifically.
source: The COH-3/4 antibody recognizes COH-3 and COH-4 specifically, since staining was undetectable in coh-4 coh-3 double mutants, but strong staining persisted in both single mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), as expected from the complete genetic redundancy of the coh-4 and coh-3 genes (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing absence of staining in double mutants but presence in single mutants.

claim: COH-3/4 and REC-8 bind chromosomes independently of each other.
source: Long tracks of COH-3/4 (Figure 1B) and SMC-3 (Figure 1D; Chan et al., 2003) staining were evident on meiotic chromosomes of rec-8 single mutants, and both REC-8 (Figure 1C) and SMC-3 (Figure 1D) persisted on chromosomes of coh-4 coh-3 mutants.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figures 1B, 1C, and 1D showing persistence of each kleisin in the absence of the other.

claim: COH-3/4 and REC-8 require SMC subunits for their chromosomal association.
source: In converse experiments, binding of REC-8 (Figure 1C) and COH-3/4 (Figure 1B) to meiotic chromosomes was severely disrupted in smc-1(RNAi) animals, as was binding of SMC-3 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figures 1B, 1C, and 1D showing loss of kleisin staining upon SMC-1 depletion.

claim: SMC-3 is nearly undetectable on meiotic chromosomes of kleisin triple mutants.
source: In contrast, SMC-3 was nearly undetectable on meiotic chromosomes of kleisin triple mutants (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: REC-8 and COH-3/4 associate with chromosomes as subunits of independent meiotic cohesin complexes that differ in their kleisin subunit.
source: These results provide strong evidence that REC-8 and COH-3/4 associate with chromosomes as subunits of independent meiotic cohesin complexes that differ in their kleisin subunit (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing independent binding of REC-8 and COH-3/4, their dependence on SMC proteins, and loss of SMC-3 in kleisin triple mutants.

claim: In proliferating cells, cohesin loads onto chromosomes prior to S phase and becomes cohesive during DNA replication.
source: In proliferating cells, cohesin loading and SCC establishment are temporally separate events: Scc1 cohesin loads onto chromosomes prior to S phase and becomes cohesive during DNA replication (Guacci et al., 1997; Michaelis et al., 1997; Losada et al., 1998; Uhlmann and Nasmyth, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from multiple sources.

claim: C. elegans REC-8 cohesin accumulates before premeiotic S phase.
source: C. elegans REC-8 cohesin appears to behave similarly, since REC-8 accumulates before premeiotic S phase (Pasierbek et al., 2001; Hayashi et al., 2007; Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature and the authors' prior work.

claim: COH-3/4 become detectable during meiotic prophase, after completion of premeiotic replication.
source: To our surprise, COH-3/4 cohesin behaves differently: COH-3/4 become detectable during meiotic prophase, after completion of premeiotic replication.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1E showing absence of COH-3/4 in PCNA-positive nuclei and appearance in the transition zone.

claim: REC-8 was detected in all germ-cell nuclei of the gonad, including premeiotic nuclei.
source: As shown previously, we detected REC-8 in all germ-cell nuclei of the gonad, including premeiotic nuclei, consistent with SCC establishment in premeiotic S phase (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) (Pasierbek et al., 2001; Hayashi et al., 2007; Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, and is consistent with prior literature.

claim: COH-3/4 was not detected in premeiotic nuclei, but intense COH-3/4 staining appeared abruptly on meiotic chromosomal axes in the transition zone.
source: In contrast, COH-3/4 was not detected in premeiotic nuclei, but intense COH-3/4 staining appeared abruptly on meiotic chromosomal axes in the transition zone and persisted through prophase I, suggesting that COH-3/4 first accumulates at the onset of meiosis (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: COH-3/4 staining was not detected in nuclei that expressed PCNA.
source: First, COH-3/4 staining was not detected in nuclei that expressed PCNA, an S phase-specific DNA polymerase processivity factor used for mitotic and premeiotic DNA replication (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In glp-1 gain-of-function mutants, REC-8, but not COH-3/4, was strongly expressed in mitotically proliferating nuclei.
source: Second, in animals carrying a glp-1 gain-of-function allele that blocks the initiation of meiosis (Berry et al., 1997), REC-8, but not COH-3/4, was strongly expressed in the mitotically proliferating nuclei that filled the entire gonad (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: COH-3/4 associates with chromosomes after premeiotic S phase is complete.
source: Thus, COH-3/4 associates with chromosomes after premeiotic S phase is complete, suggesting that COH-3/4 and REC-8 cohesins may load onto chromosomes and become cohesive by different mechanisms.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing absence of COH-3/4 in PCNA-positive nuclei and in glp-1(gf) mutants.

claim: REC-8 was undetectable on meiotic chromosomes in htp-3 mutants.
source: We therefore examined COH-3/4 loading in two mutant strains in which REC-8 was undetectable on meiotic chromosomes but SCC persisted: htp-3 mutants lacking the HORMA domain AE protein HTP-3 (Goodyer et al., 2008; Severson et al., 2009), and tim-1 mutants lacking the C. elegans TIMELESS homolog TIM-1 (Chan et al., 2003) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: REC-8 was undetectable on meiotic chromosomes in tim-1 mutants.
source: We therefore examined COH-3/4 loading in two mutant strains in which REC-8 was undetectable on meiotic chromosomes but SCC persisted: htp-3 mutants lacking the HORMA domain AE protein HTP-3 (Goodyer et al., 2008; Severson et al., 2009), and tim-1 mutants lacking the C. elegans TIMELESS homolog TIM-1 (Chan et al., 2003) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: COH-3/4 loading appeared normal in htp-3 and tim-1 mutants.
source: In contrast, COH-3/4 loading appeared normal in htp-3 and tim-1 mutants (Figure 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The kleisin subunit specifies the mechanism by which a cohesin complex initially associates with meiotic chromosomes.
source: Thus, specific factors likely promote the differential loading of cohesin complexes, and the kleisin subunit specifies the mechanism by which a complex initially associates with meiotic chromosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing differential requirements for HTP-3 and TIM-1 in loading REC-8 versus COH-3/4.

claim: A single GFP focus was detected in 100% of diakinesis nuclei of wild-type worms.
source: As expected, a single GFP focus was detected in 100% of diakinesis nuclei of wild-type worms and coh-4 coh-3 double mutants (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), consistent with the finding that REC-8 cohesin is sufficient to tether and co-orient sister chromatids (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3C and quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A single GFP focus was detected in 100% of diakinesis nuclei of coh-4 coh-3 double mutants.
source: As expected, a single GFP focus was detected in 100% of diakinesis nuclei of wild-type worms and coh-4 coh-3 double mutants (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), consistent with the finding that REC-8 cohesin is sufficient to tether and co-orient sister chromatids (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3D and quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two discrete GFP foci could usually be detected within univalents in diakinesis nuclei of rec-8 worms.
source: LacI::GFP also labeled a single detached homolog (univalent) in most diakinesis nuclei of rec-8 worms; however, two discrete GFP foci could usually be detected within the univalent (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3C and quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In 84% of rec-8 nuclei, either a single GFP focus was detected or two foci were detected within one univalent at a spacing of ≤1.5 µm.
source: In 84% of rec-8 nuclei, either a single GFP focus was detected or two foci were detected within one univalent at a spacing of ≤1.5 µm (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Only 10% of diakinesis nuclei in kleisin triple mutants had LacI::GFP foci separated by ≤ 1.5 µm.
source: In contrast, only 10% of diakinesis nuclei in kleisin triple mutants had LacI::GFP foci separated by ≤ 1.5 µm (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2) (Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Sisters were apart in 90% of diakinesis nuclei of spo-11 rec-8 double mutants.
source: We found sisters to be apart in 90% of diakinesis nuclei of spo-11 rec-8 double mutants, indicating that COH-3/4 requires SPO-11 to tether sister chromatids (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Sisters could not be resolved in any nuclei of spo-11; coh-4 coh-3 triple mutants.
source: In contrast, sisters could not be resolved in any nuclei of spo-11; coh-4 coh-3 triple mutants, indicating that REC-8 cohesin becomes cohesive independently of SPO-11 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The SCC disruption in spo-11 rec-8 mutants did not result from a defect in COH-3/4 cohesin loading.
source: The SCC disruption in spo-11 rec-8 mutants did not result from a defect in COH-3/4 cohesin loading, since levels of bound COH-3/4 were similar in wild-type animals, spo-11 rec-8 double mutants, and spo-11 or rec-8 single mutants (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 12 Gy of γ-irradiation triggered crossover recombination between most homolog pairs of spo-11 mutants without causing chromosomal fragmentation or fusion.
source: Prior experiments showed that γ-irradiation restored CO recombination in spo-11 mutants and suppressed lethality (Dernburg et al., 1998). In our experiments, 12 Gy of γ-irradiation triggered CO recombination between most homolog pairs of spo-11 mutants without causing chromosomal fragmentation or fusion (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is directly observed in the data shown in Figure 3E, and is consistent with prior literature (Dernburg et al., 1998).

claim: γ-irradiation restored sister chromatid cohesion in spo-11 rec-8 double mutants.
source: That dose also restored SCC: sisters were tethered in 75% of irradiated spo-11 rec-8 double mutants (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Programmed meiotic DSBs are essential for COH-3/4-dependent sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Thus, programmed meiotic DSBs are essential for COH-3/4-dependent SCC, and the kleisin subunit determines whether a cohesin requires DSBs to establish cohesion.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing loss of SCC in spo-11 rec-8 mutants and restoration by γ-irradiation.

claim: In yeast G2/M phase, DNA breaks activate the Mec1/ATR kinase, which stimulates the Chk1 kinase to phosphorylate the mitotic kleisin Scc1 on serine 83, triggering cohesin to become cohesive.
source: In the yeast model for DSB-induced SCC (DI-SCC), DNA breaks activate the Mec1/ATR kinase. Mec1 in turn stimulates the Chk1 kinase to phosphorylate the mitotic kleisin Scc1 on serine 83, which triggers cohesin to become cohesive (Figure 3A; Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008.

claim: Yeast Rec8 lacks the Chk kinase phosphorylation site and consequently cannot become cohesive in response to DNA damage.
source: Yeast Rec8 lacks the Chk kinase phosphorylation site and consequently cannot become cohesive in response to DNA damage.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008.

claim: Sisters were apart in 59% of diakinesis nuclei in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1(RNAi) mutants.
source: Sisters were apart in 59% of diakinesis nuclei in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1(RNAi) mutants (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: The SCC defects in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1(RNAi) mutants did not result from impaired COH-3/4 cohesin loading.
source: Importantly, the SCC defects in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1(RNAi) mutants did not result from impaired COH-3/4 cohesin loading (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Sisters were always tethered in coh-4 coh-3 mutants deficient in ATM-1 and ATL-1.
source: Furthermore, sisters were always tethered in coh-4 coh-3 mutants deficient in ATM-1 and ATL-1 (100%, Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ATM-1 and ATL-1 are required to trigger the cohesiveness of COH-3/4 cohesin, but not REC-8 cohesin.
source: We conclude that ATM-1 and ATL-1 are required to trigger the cohesiveness of COH-3/4 cohesin, but not REC-8 cohesin.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing SCC defects in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 mutants but not in atm-1; coh-4 coh-3; atl-1 mutants.

claim: Diakinesis nuclei of rec-8; chk-1(RNAi) worms had 12 univalents, and LacI::GFP staining showed no sister separation.
source: Diakinesis nuclei of rec-8; chk-1(RNAi) worms had 12 univalents, and LacI::GFP staining showed no sister separation, indicating that CHK-1 kinase is not required (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Sisters were apart in 100% of rec-8; chk-2 nuclei.
source: In contrast, sisters were apart in 100% of rec-8; chk-2 nuclei (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplements 2, 3 and 3B).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplements 2, 3, and 3B.

claim: Exposure of rec-8; chk-2 mutants to γ-irradiation failed to restore sister chromatid cohesion.
source: However, exposure of rec-8; chk-2 mutants to the dose of γ-irradiation that restored SCC in spo-11 rec-8 worms failed to restore SCC in rec-8; chk-2 mutants. Sisters remained apart (100%), and chromosome fragments were evident, indicating defective repair of DSBs by homologous recombination (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: DSBs, ATM-1/ATL-1 and CHK-2, but not CHK-1, are required for COH-3/4-dependent sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Thus, DSBs, ATM-1/ATL-1 and CHK-2, but not CHK-1, are required for COH-3/4-dependent SCC.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing SCC defects in spo-11 rec-8, atm-1; rec-8; atl-1, and rec-8; chk-2 mutants, but not in rec-8; chk-1 mutants.

claim: A conserved pathway establishes sister chromatid cohesion in response to DSBs in yeast mitosis and in C. elegans meiosis.
source: Our results provide strong evidence that a conserved pathway establishes SCC in response to DSBs in yeast mitosis and in C. elegans meiosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity between the yeast DI-SCC pathway (Mec1/ATR → Chk1 → Scc1 phosphorylation) and the C. elegans pathway (ATM-1/ATL-1 → CHK-2 → COH-3/4).

claim: In most pachytene nuclei of wild-type worms, rec-8 single mutants, and coh-4 coh-3 double mutants, sisters were tethered.
source: In most pachytene nuclei of wild-type worms (>99%), rec-8 single mutants (95%), and coh-4 coh-3 double mutants (>99%), sisters were tethered (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sisters were apart in 55% of pachytene nuclei of meiotic kleisin triple mutants.
source: In contrast, sisters were apart in most nuclei of meiotic kleisin triple mutants (55%), revealing that REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins establish SCC.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Linkages persisted in 45% of pachytene nuclei in kleisin triple mutants, indicating that factors other than REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins can also tether sisters.
source: However, the persistence of linkages in 45% of pachytene nuclei in kleisin triple mutants indicated that factors other than REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins can also tether sisters (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The C. elegans mitotic kleisin SCC-1 contributes to cohesion in pachytene nuclei.
source: We found that the C. elegans mitotic kleisin SCC-1, previously thought to function only during mitosis, contributes to cohesion in pachytene nuclei (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the increased sister separation in kleisin triple mutants depleted of SCC-1 compared to kleisin triple mutants with wild-type SCC-1 levels (Figure 5A,B).

claim: Only 12% of pachytene nuclei exhibited cohesion in SCC-1-depleted kleisin triple mutants.
source: Only 12% of pachytene nuclei exhibited cohesion in SCC-1-depleted kleisin triple mutants, indicating that SCC-1 cohesin can mediate REC-8 and COH-3/4-independent linkages (Figure 5 A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: SCC-1 associates with axial structures of transition zone and pachytene nuclei of wild-type animals.
source: Consistent with the involvement of SCC-1 cohesin in tethering chromosomes during pachytene but not diakinesis, we observed that SCC-1 associates with axial structures of transition zone and pachytene nuclei of wild-type animals (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SCC-1 was undetectable on chromosomes following nuclear envelope breakdown.
source: Diffuse nuclear staining obscured any chromosomal signal in diplotene/diakinesis nuclei; however, SCC-1 was undetectable on chromosomes following nuclear envelope breakdown, when the nucleoplasmic signal dissipated.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The absence of DSBs in spo-11 rec-8 animals did not abrogate sister chromatid cohesion in pachytene nuclei.
source: Unexpectedly, the absence of DSBs in spo-11 rec-8 animals did not abrogate SCC in pachytene nuclei (6.8% lacking SCC), unlike in diakinesis nuclei (90% lacking SCC); however, we reasoned that axial element proteins and synaptonemal complex (SC) proteins (Figure 5E) might mediate the linkages that persist between sisters in pachytene nuclei of spo-11 rec-8 mutants and thereby obscure the role of DSBs.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Sister chromatids were apart in ∼70% of pachytene nuclei of him-3 rec-8 animals.
source: SCC was severely compromised in pachytene nuclei of animals lacking REC-8 and AE protein HIM-3. Sister chromatids were apart in ∼70% of pachytene nuclei of him-3 rec-8 animals regardless of whether DSBs were made (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3), suggesting the involvement of AE proteins in tethering sister chromatids.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Abundant RAD-51 foci were found in him-3 rec-8 mutants in early and late pachytene.
source: Using RAD-51, a RecA homolog that binds to nascent recombination intermediates just after DSB formation, as a marker for DSBs, we found abundant RAD-51 foci in him-3 rec-8 mutants in early and late pachytene (Figure 4B,C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B,C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: COH-3/4 associated with meiotic chromosomes of him-3 rec-8 animals.
source: Furthermore, COH-3/4 associated with meiotic chromosomes of him-3 rec-8 animals, although the intensity of the COH-3/4 signal was less than that in wild-type animals due to defective synapsis and SCC (Figure 4A and legend and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Disrupting SYP-1 further reduces sister chromatid cohesion in spo-11 rec-8 animals.
source: We also discovered that disrupting the gene encoding the SC central region protein SYP-1 further reduces SCC in spo-11 rec-8 animals (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: In spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 triple mutants, 36% of pachytene nuclei lacked sister chromatid cohesion.
source: In spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 triple mutants, 36% of pachytene nuclei lacked SCC compared to 7% of nuclei in spo-11 rec-8 double mutants and 71% of nuclei in him-3 spo-11 rec-8, indicating that SYP-1 assists in linking sisters independently of cohesin, but AE protein HIM-3 plays a more prominent role.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: The frequency of sister separation in spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 triple mutants (36%) was greater than in rec-8; syp-1 double mutants (14%).
source: We found that the frequency of sister separation in spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 triple mutants (36%) was greater than in rec-8; syp-1 double mutants (14%) (p < 0.001) indicating that DSBs play an important role in triggering COH-3/4-dependent SCC (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3, with statistical analysis.

claim: While 0% of atm-1; coh-4 coh-3; atl-1 mutants showed sister separation in pachytene nuclei, 21% of atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 mutants exhibited separation.
source: Indeed, while 0% of atm-1; coh-4 coh-3; atl-1 mutants showed sister separation in pachytene nuclei, 21% of atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 mutants exhibited separation (p < 0.001) (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3, with statistical analysis.

claim: DSBs trigger COH-3/4 to become cohesive.
source: These results indicate that DSBs trigger COH-3/4 to become cohesive.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing increased sister separation in spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 mutants compared to rec-8; syp-1 mutants, and in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 mutants compared to atm-1; coh-4 coh-3; atl-1 mutants.

claim: Chromosome fragments and fusions were found in 100% of nuclei in animals with severely compromised REC-8- and COH-3/4-dependent sister chromatid cohesion.
source: As expected, we found chromosome fragments and fusions in 100% of nuclei in animals with severely compromised REC-8- and COH-3/4-dependent SCC (e.g. him-3 rec-8 and atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 mutants) as a consequence of defective DSB repair (Figure 3F; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 4D.

claim: Very few RAD-51 foci and virtually no chromosome fragments or fusions were found in meiotic kleisin triple mutants.
source: Unexpectedly, we found very few RAD-51 foci (Figure 4B,C) and virtually no chromosome fragments or fusions (Figure 3D and Figure 4D) in all 30 of the gonads examined from meiotic kleisin triple mutants, suggesting a nearly complete absence of early DSB repair intermediates and little or no defective DSB repair.
evidence: This is directly observed in the data shown in Figure 4B,C, Figure 3D, and Figure 4D.

claim: Cohesin is necessary for the timely formation of RAD-51 foci, and likely DSBs.
source: We conclude that cohesin, but not SCC per se, is necessary for the timely formation of RAD-51 foci, and likely DSBs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that kleisin triple mutants have very few RAD-51 foci despite having chromosomes, while him-3 rec-8 mutants with defective SCC have abundant RAD-51 foci.

claim: A single, asymmetrically positioned crossover forms between each homolog pair in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, a single, asymmetrically positioned CO forms between each homolog pair.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Barnes et al., 1995; Albertson et al., 1997; Nabeshima et al., 2005.

claim: The crossover divides each homolog pair into long and short arms.
source: The CO divides the pair into long and short arms (Barnes et al., 1995; Albertson et al., 1997; Nabeshima et al., 2005) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Barnes et al., 1995; Albertson et al., 1997; Nabeshima et al., 2005.

claim: Co-orientation occurs at the long arms to ensure that the two sister chromatids interact with microtubules from the same spindle pole.
source: Co-orientation occurs at the long arms to ensure that the two sister chromatids interact with microtubules from the same spindle pole, and SCC is maintained at the long arms until anaphase II to keep sisters together.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, reviewed in Schvarzstein et al., 2010.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion is maintained at the long arms until anaphase II to keep sisters together.
source: Co-orientation occurs at the long arms to ensure that the two sister chromatids interact with microtubules from the same spindle pole, and SCC is maintained at the long arms until anaphase II to keep sisters together.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, reviewed in Schvarzstein et al., 2010.

claim: Cohesion at the short arms holds homologs together, and sister chromatid cohesion release at short arms in anaphase I triggers disjunction of homologous chromosomes.
source: Cohesion at the short arms holds homologs together, and SCC release at short arms in anaphase I triggers disjunction of homologous chromosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, reviewed in Schvarzstein et al., 2010.

claim: COH-3/4 was removed from the long arm and became restricted to the short arm by prometaphase.
source: We found that during this reorganization, COH-3/4 was removed from the long arm and became restricted to the short arm by prometaphase (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: REC-8 is progressively removed from the short arm of diakinesis bivalents and often becomes undetectable by metaphase I.
source: We confirmed that REC-8 is progressively removed from the short arm of diakinesis bivalents and often becomes undetectable by metaphase I (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B, and is consistent with prior observations (de Carvalho et al., 2008; Harper et al., 2011; Rogers et al., 2002).

claim: The redistribution of COH-3/4 precedes that of REC-8.
source: The redistribution of COH-3/4 precedes that of REC-8, which is usually not apparent until late diakinesis or prometaphase I (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The kleisin subunit determines both when and where a cohesin complex will be removed from chromosomes during late prophase and prometaphase.
source: Thus, the kleisin subunit determines both when and where a cohesin complex will be removed from chromosomes during late prophase and prometaphase.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that COH-3/4 is removed from long arms in diplotene while REC-8 is removed from short arms in late diakinesis/prometaphase.

claim: REC-8 and COH-3/4 persist along the entire axis of desynapsing chromosomes in diplotene nuclei of spo-11 mutants.
source: Indeed, REC-8 and COH-3/4 persist along the entire axis of desynapsing chromosomes in diplotene nuclei of spo-11 mutants (Figure 7A), and both kleisins associate with the midunivalent of the detached homologs in diakinesis nuclei (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Removal of REC-8 from the short arm did not require the worm separase homolog SEP-1.
source: Consistent with this, removal of REC-8 from the short arm did not require the worm separase homolog SEP-1 (Figure 7B) but did require the Aurora B kinase AIR-2, which accumulates at the short arm in late diakinesis, prior to the reduction of REC-8 in this region (Figure 7C,D; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Removal of REC-8 from the short arm required the Aurora B kinase AIR-2.
source: Consistent with this, removal of REC-8 from the short arm did not require the worm separase homolog SEP-1 (Figure 7B) but did require the Aurora B kinase AIR-2, which accumulates at the short arm in late diakinesis, prior to the reduction of REC-8 in this region (Figure 7C,D; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7C,D, and is consistent with prior literature (Rogers et al., 2002).

claim: Dissociation of COH-3/4 from the long arm was independent of SEP-1.
source: Dissociation of COH-3/4 from the long arm was also independent of SEP-1.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Neither removal of COH-3/4 from the long arm nor maintenance of COH-3/4 at the short arm required AIR-2.
source: However, neither removal of COH-3/4 from the long arm nor maintenance of COH-3/4 at the short arm required AIR-2 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The kleisin determines not only when and where, but also how a cohesin complex is removed from chromosomes.
source: Thus, the kleisin determines not only when and where, but also how a cohesin complex is removed from chromosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that REC-8 removal requires AIR-2 while COH-3/4 removal does not.

claim: The kleisin influences nearly all aspects of meiotic cohesin function.
source: We showed that multiple, functionally distinct cohesin complexes mediate sister chromatid cohesion during meiosis. The cohesins differ in their α-kleisin subunit, and the kleisin influences nearly all aspects of meiotic cohesin function: the mechanisms for loading cohesins onto chromosomes, for triggering DNA-bound cohesins to become cohesive, and for releasing cohesins in a temporal- and location-specific manner during prophase I.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by all the data in the manuscript showing differential loading (Figure 2), differential timing of accumulation (Figure 1E), differential mechanisms of SCC establishment (Figure 3), and differential removal patterns (Figure 6B, Figure 7).

claim: DSB-induced tethering of sister chromatids is an essential feature of meiosis.
source: Thus, DSB-induced SCC is an essential, conserved process that functions not only in proliferating yeast cells suffering DNA damage, but also in nematode germ cells undergoing normal gametogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that COH-3/4-mediated SCC requires SPO-11-dependent DSBs and can be restored by γ-irradiation.

claim: Axial element protein HIM-3 can tether sisters in pachytene nuclei independently of REC-8 in both rec-8 single and spo-11 rec-8 double mutants.
source: Second, the AE protein HIM-3 can tether sisters in pachytene nuclei independently of REC-8 in both rec-8 single and spo-11 rec-8 double mutants, thereby obscuring the role of DSBs in establishing COH-3/4-mediated SCC.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that sisters are together in most pachytene nuclei of spo-11 rec-8 mutants, but apart in him-3 rec-8 mutants.

claim: Synaptonemal complexes form between sisters in rec-8 and spo-11 rec-8 animals.
source: Third, synaptonemal complexes form between sisters in rec-8 and spo-11 rec-8 animals.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Disrupting DSB formation in rec-8 mutants lacking the SC central region protein SYP-1 increased the frequency of sister separation in pachytene nuclei relative to that of rec-8; syp-1 double mutants proficient in DSB formation.
source: Disrupting DSB formation in rec-8 mutants lacking the SC central region protein SYP-1 (i.e., spo-11 rec-8; syp-1 triple mutants) increased the frequency of sister separation in pachytene nuclei relative to that of rec-8; syp-1 double mutants proficient in DSB formation.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: Sister separation is greater in pachytene nuclei of rec-8 mutants with a defective ATM/ATR signaling pathway than in rec-8 mutants with a functional pathway.
source: Finally, sister separation is greater in pachytene nuclei of rec-8 mutants with a defective ATM/ATR signaling pathway than in rec-8 mutants with a functional pathway.
evidence: This is quantified from the LacI::GFP assay data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplements 2 and 3.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DNA damage in G2/M activates ATM and Chk1 kinases, leading to Chk1-dependent phosphorylation of Scc1 on serine 83.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, DNA damage in G2/M activates ATM and Chk1 kinases, leading to Chk1-dependent phosphorylation of Scc1 on serine 83.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008, 2009.

claim: Unphosphorylatable S83A mutants of yeast Scc1 fail to establish damage-induced sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Unphosphorylatable S83A mutants fail to establish DI-SCC, while phosphomimetic S83D mutants establish DI-SCC independently of Chk1, showing the importance of S83 phosphorylation in inducing cohesion in response to DNA damage (Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2009, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008, 2009.

claim: Phosphomimetic S83D mutants of yeast Scc1 establish damage-induced sister chromatid cohesion independently of Chk1.
source: Unphosphorylatable S83A mutants fail to establish DI-SCC, while phosphomimetic S83D mutants establish DI-SCC independently of Chk1, showing the importance of S83 phosphorylation in inducing cohesion in response to DNA damage (Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2009, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Heidinger-Pauli et al., 2008, 2009.

claim: SPO-11-dependent DSBs activate a signaling cascade to trigger meiotic damage-induced sister chromatid cohesion through COH-3/4 cohesin in C. elegans.
source: SPO-11-dependent DSBs appear to activate a similar signaling cascade to trigger meiotic DI-SCC through COH-3/4 cohesin in C. elegans.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that COH-3/4-mediated SCC requires SPO-11, ATM-1/ATL-1, and CHK-2.

claim: The signaling cascade that triggers COH-3/4-mediated sister chromatid cohesion requires ATM, ATR, and CHK-2.
source: This cascade requires ATM, ATR, and CHK-2 and likely culminates in kleisin phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing SCC defects in atm-1; rec-8; atl-1 and rec-8; chk-2 mutants.

claim: CHK-2 may function in regulating cohesin loading as well as in triggering sister linkages.
source: Because rec-8; chk-2 mutants exhibited reduced COH-3/4 staining and complete failure to tether sisters, CHK-2 may function in regulating cohesin loading as well as in triggering sister linkages.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that rec-8; chk-2 mutants have reduced COH-3/4 staining compared to other mutants.

claim: Robust synaptonemal complex assembled along chromosomes of spo-11 rec-8 mutants.
source: Robust SC assembled along chromosomes of spo-11 rec-8 mutants, between sister chromatids or non-homologous chromosomes, but SC assembly failed on chromosomes of kleisin triple mutants.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Synaptonemal complex assembly failed on chromosomes of kleisin triple mutants.
source: Robust SC assembled along chromosomes of spo-11 rec-8 mutants, between sister chromatids or non-homologous chromosomes, but SC assembly failed on chromosomes of kleisin triple mutants.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Synaptonemal complex assembly requires COH-3/4 binding but not its conversion to a cohesive state.
source: Thus, SC assembly requires COH-3/4 binding but not its conversion to a cohesive state, revealing that cohesin functions in cohesion-independent processes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SC assembles in spo-11 rec-8 mutants (which have COH-3/4 binding but not COH-3/4-mediated cohesion) but not in kleisin triple mutants (which lack COH-3/4 binding).

claim: Synaptonemal complex assembly is more sensitive to disruption of COH-3/4 cohesin than REC-8 cohesin.
source: These data also demonstrated that SC assembly is more sensitive to disruption of COH-3/4 cohesin than REC-8 cohesin, since we observed severe SC structural defects in coh-4 coh-3 double mutants but not in rec-8 single mutants (See also Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of SC defects in coh-4 coh-3 mutants but not in rec-8 mutants, as shown in prior work (Severson et al., 2009).

claim: Weak linkages can occur between sisters in pachytene nuclei of mutants lacking the three meiotic kleisins.
source: In contrast, although REC-8 and COH-3/4 are critical for establishing meiotic SCC, weak linkages can occur between sisters in pachytene nuclei of mutants lacking the three meiotic kleisins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that 45% of pachytene nuclei in kleisin triple mutants still have sisters together.

claim: SCC-1 cohesin can mediate weak linkages between sisters in pachytene nuclei of kleisin triple mutants.
source: These linkages are mediated by SCC-1 cohesin, previously believed to function only during mitosis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the increased sister separation in kleisin triple mutants depleted of SCC-1.

claim: SCC-1 by itself is not likely to establish sister chromatid cohesion in wild-type animals.
source: However, the finding that two LacI::GFP foci could be resolved in ∼89% of pachytene nuclei of kleisin triple mutants with wild-type levels of SCC-1 demonstrates that, unlike SCC mediated by REC-8 or COH-3/4 cohesin, SCC mediated by SCC-1 cohesin is insufficient to maintain the close association of sisters along their entire lengths. Thus, SCC-1 by itself is not likely to establish SCC in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that sisters can be resolved in most pachytene nuclei of kleisin triple mutants with wild-type SCC-1 levels.

claim: Mitotic kleisins associate with meiotic chromosomes of budding yeast and mice.
source: Mitotic kleisins also associate with meiotic chromosomes of budding yeast and mice (Klein et al., 1999; Xu et al., 2004; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from multiple sources.

claim: The Rad54 paralog Tid1 is necessary to remove Scc1-dependent linkages from yeast meiotic chromosomes to facilitate normal chromosome segregation.
source: The Rad54 paralog Tid1 is necessary to remove Scc1-dependent linkages from yeast meiotic chromosomes to facilitate normal chromosome segregation (Kateneva et al., 2005), indicating that Scc1 cohesin can tether sisters during meiosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research in yeast, cited from Kateneva et al., 2005.

claim: Synaptonemal complex proteins do not associate with meiotic chromosomes in pachytene nuclei of rec-8; coh-4 coh-3 mutants where SCC-1 tethers sisters.
source: Although SCC-1 can tether sisters in pachytene nuclei of rec-8; coh-4 coh-3 mutants, SC proteins do not associate with meiotic chromosomes.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Establishment of cohesion between sisters is insufficient to promote the formation of synaptonemal complex.
source: These data demonstrate that establishment of cohesion between sisters is insufficient to promote the formation of SC, consistent with our finding that SC assembly requires chromosomally bound COH-3/4 cohesin, but not conversion of COH-3/4 cohesin into a cohesive state.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SCC-1 can tether sisters in kleisin triple mutants but SC does not assemble.

claim: HIM-3 tethers sisters independently of cohesin in spo-11 rec-8 mutants.
source: That is, HIM-3 tethers sisters independently of cohesin in spo-11 rec-8 mutants, which have chromosome-bound COH-3/4 that is not cohesive.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing severe SCC defects in him-3 rec-8 mutants compared to rec-8 single mutants.

claim: HIM-3-dependent linkages are not mediated by a synaptonemal complex-like structure.
source: The HIM-3-dependent linkages are not mediated by an SC-like structure, given that disrupting the CR protein SYP-1 only partially weakened SCC in spo-11 rec-8 double mutants, while mutations in him-3 severely abrogated SCC.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of SCC defects in him-3 rec-8 mutants versus rec-8; syp-1 mutants.

claim: HIM-3-dependent linkages may prevent newly replicated sister chromatids from drifting apart in rec-8 mutants before DSBs trigger COH-3/4 to become cohesive.
source: However, HIM-3-dependent linkages may prevent newly replicated sister chromatids from drifting apart in rec-8 mutants before DSBs trigger COH-3/4 to become cohesive, thus explaining the severe SCC defects observed in him-3 rec-8 double mutants with wild-type spo-11.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of severe SCC defects in him-3 rec-8 mutants.

claim: Purified yeast Hop1 can mediate trans interactions that bridge linear double-stranded DNA molecules and promote their restructuring and compaction.
source: Single molecule experiments have shown that purified Hop1, a HORMA domain protein that is the yeast ortholog of HIM-3, HTP-3, and HTP-1/2, can mediate trans interactions that bridge linear double-stranded DNA molecules and promote their restructuring and compaction (Khan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Khan et al., 2012.

claim: HORMA-domain axial element proteins such as HIM-3 may directly tether sister chromatids independently of cohesin in wild-type animals.
source: These interactions were proposed to facilitate pairing or synapsis of homologous chromosomes, but our data suggest a different role: HORMA-domain AE proteins such as HIM-3 may directly tether sister chromatids independently of cohesin in wild-type animals, as we have shown for cohesion-defective mutants.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data showing HIM-3-dependent sister tethering in rec-8 mutants and the known biochemical properties of Hop1.

claim: REC-8 cohesin mediates the first wave of sister chromatid cohesion establishment.
source: Our data support the following model. REC-8 cohesin mediates the first wave of SCC establishment.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing REC-8 accumulation before premeiotic S phase.

claim: SCC-1 may function together with REC-8 during the first wave of sister chromatid cohesion establishment.
source: SCC-1 may function together with REC-8 during that process.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that SCC-1 is present in premeiotic nuclei and can mediate weak linkages.

claim: REC-8 and SCC-1 are present in all premeiotic nuclei and likely bind to chromatids prior to premeiotic S phase and become cohesive during DNA replication.
source: Both REC-8 and SCC-1 are present in all premeiotic nuclei and likely bind to chromatids prior to premeiotic S phase and become cohesive during DNA replication, a pattern similar to that described for cohesin complexes in mitotically proliferating cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunofluorescence data showing REC-8 and SCC-1 in premeiotic nuclei, combined with established knowledge of cohesin behavior in mitosis.

claim: HIM-3 may mediate a second wave of cohesion through a mechanism distinct from that of cohesin.
source: HIM-3 may mediate a second wave of cohesion, but through a mechanism distinct from that of cohesin.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data showing HIM-3-dependent sister tethering independently of cohesin.

claim: HIM-3 is expressed and loads onto chromosomes in leptotene, at the onset of meiosis.
source: HIM-3 is expressed and loads onto chromosomes in leptotene, at the onset of meiosis (Zetka et al., 1999; MacQueen et al., 2002), and our data suggest that HIM-3 tethers sisters independently of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Zetka et al., 1999; MacQueen et al., 2002.

claim: A final wave of sister chromatid cohesion establishment is mediated by COH-3/4 cohesin, which loads onto chromosomes at the onset of meiosis but is not triggered to become cohesive until the formation of SPO-11-dependent DSBs.
source: A final wave of SCC establishment is mediated by COH-3/4 cohesin, which loads onto chromosomes at the onset of meiosis but is not triggered to become cohesive until the formation of SPO-11-dependent DSBs during leptotene and/or zygotene.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing COH-3/4 accumulation in the transition zone and requirement for SPO-11 to establish COH-3/4-mediated SCC.

claim: In diplotene and diakinesis nuclei, sisters are held together by REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin alone.
source: Our data also suggest that the removal of linkages between sisters occurs in stages. In diplotene (our unpublished data) and diakinesis nuclei, sisters are held together by REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesin alone, indicating that the HIM-3 and SCC-1-dependent linkages we demonstrated in pachytene are transient and are removed during late pachytene or early diplotene.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that sisters are apart in diakinesis nuclei of kleisin triple mutants but together in pachytene nuclei.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion mediated by COH-3/4 persists until anaphase I.
source: In contrast, SCC mediated by COH-3/4 and REC-8 persists until anaphase I and II, respectively (see below).
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotype of rec-8 mutants where sisters separate at anaphase I, indicating that COH-3/4-mediated SCC persists until anaphase I.

claim: Sister chromatid cohesion mediated by REC-8 persists until anaphase II.
source: In contrast, SCC mediated by COH-3/4 and REC-8 persists until anaphase I and II, respectively (see below).
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotype of coh-4 coh-3 mutants where sisters remain together until anaphase II.

claim: Prior models asserted that the stepwise cleavage of Rec8 by separase initiated the successive separation of homologs and sisters.
source: Prior to this study and our earlier demonstration that COH-3/4 and REC-8 mediate meiotic SCC (Severson et al., 2009), the triggering and release of meiotic cohesion were thought to depend entirely on Rec8 cohesin. All models of eukaryotic meiotic chromosome segregation asserted that the stepwise cleavage of Rec8 by separase initiated the successive separation of homologs and sisters, and thus the production of haploid gametes.
evidence: This is a summary of prior models in the field, based on established knowledge.

claim: In organisms with monocentric chromosomes, cleavage of Rec8 along chromosome arms was proposed to trigger homolog separation in meiosis I.
source: In organisms with monocentric chromosomes, cleavage of Rec8 along chromosome arms was proposed to trigger homolog separation in meiosis I, while cleavage of Rec8 at centromeres was proposed to allow sister separation in meiosis II (Klein et al., 1999; Watanabe and Nurse, 1999; Buonomo et al., 2000; Watanabe, 2004; Kudo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a summary of prior models in the field, cited from multiple sources.

claim: In C. elegans, cleavage of REC-8 at the short arm was believed to elicit homolog segregation in meiosis I.
source: In the holocentric nematode C. elegans, where the asymmetric CO site rather than the centromere defines the bivalent short and long arms, cleavage of REC-8 at the short arm was believed to elicit homolog segregation in meiosis I, while cleavage of REC-8 at the bivalent long arm was believed to cause sister separation in meiosis II (Pasierbek et al., 2001; Siomos et al., 2001; Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a summary of prior models for C. elegans, cited from multiple sources.

claim: AIR-2 accumulates at bivalent short arms and is essential for homolog separation in meiosis I.
source: Consistent with this model, prior C. elegans studies identified the Aurora B kinase AIR-2 as a key factor that regulates SCC release, and thus chromosome segregation, during meiosis and mitosis. In meiosis I, AIR-2 accumulates at bivalent short arms and is essential for homolog separation (Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: In meiosis II, AIR-2 accumulates between sisters and is required for sister separation.
source: In meiosis II, AIR-2 accumulates between sisters and is required for sister separation.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: AIR-2 can phosphorylate REC-8 in vitro.
source: AIR-2 can phosphorylate REC-8 in vitro (Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: AIR-2 is prevented from accumulating at the long arms during meiosis I by HTP-1/2 and LAB-1.
source: AIR-2 is prevented from accumulating at the long arms during meiosis I by the partially redundant AE proteins HTP-1 and HTP-2 (HTP-1/2) and the novel, Caenorhabditis-specific protein LAB-1 (de Carvalho et al., 2008; Kaitna et al., 2002; Martinez-Perez et al., 2008; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from multiple sources.

claim: Crossover recombination triggers removal of HTP-1/2 and LAB-1 from short arms, allowing the accumulation of AIR-2 at the short arms.
source: HTP-1/2 and LAB-1 accumulate along the entire length of meiotic chromosomal axes in early pachytene, but CO recombination triggers their removal from short arms and thereby allows the accumulation of AIR-2 at the short arms.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from de Carvalho et al., 2008; Kaitna et al., 2002; Martinez-Perez et al., 2008; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: HTP-1/2 and LAB-1 are undetectable on chromosomes after anaphase I.
source: HTP-1/2 and LAB-1 are undetectable on chromosomes after anaphase I; consequently, AIR-2 accumulates between sisters in meiosis II.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from de Carvalho et al., 2008; Kaitna et al., 2002; Martinez-Perez et al., 2008; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: In htp-1 htp-2 and lab-1 mutants, AIR-2 associates with both long and short arms, and sister chromatids separate prematurely during anaphase I.
source: In htp-1 htp-2 and lab-1 mutants, AIR-2 associates with both long and short arms. As a consequence, sister chromatids separate prematurely during anaphase I.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, cited from de Carvalho et al., 2008; Kaitna et al., 2002; Martinez-Perez et al., 2008; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: Prior models proposed that AIR-2 induces the stepwise separation of homologs and sisters by phosphorylating REC-8, first at the short arm to trigger separase-dependent cleavage in anaphase I, then at the long arm to trigger separase-mediated cleavage in anaphase II.
source: The correlation between the presence of AIR-2 and the release of SCC during meiosis of wild-type animals and htp-1 htp-2 and lab-1 mutants, together with the finding that AIR-2 can phosphorylate REC-8 in vitro, led to the model that AIR-2 induces the stepwise separation of homologs and sisters by phosphorylating REC-8, first at the short arm to trigger separase-dependent cleavage in anaphase I, then at the long arm to trigger separase-mediated cleavage in anaphase II (Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a summary of prior models in the field, cited from Kaitna et al., 2002; Rogers et al., 2002.

claim: It has never been determined whether AIR-2-dependent phosphorylation is required for separase to cleave REC-8.
source: However, it has never been determined whether AIR-2-dependent phosphorylation is required for separase to cleave REC-8 or whether cleavage of REC-8 by separase is required for homolog separation at anaphase I.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior research.

claim: Prior models are insufficient to explain how linkages are removed between sister chromatids to permit the separation of homologs and then sisters.
source: Together, our discovery of COH-3/4 in C. elegans and our demonstration that CO recombination consistently triggers separase-independent removal of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins from reciprocal domains of meiosis I bivalents indicate that prior models are insufficient to explain how linkages are removed between sister chromatids to permit the separation of homologs and then sisters.
evidence: This is inferred from the new data showing separase-independent cohesin removal and the existence of multiple meiotic kleisins.

claim: Any model of C. elegans meiotic chromosome segregation must incorporate the removal of REC-8 cohesin by separase, the separase-dependent removal of COH-3/4 cohesin, and the role of separase-independent cohesin removal that occurs in late prophase.
source: Any model of C. elegans meiotic chromosome segregation must incorporate not only the removal of REC-8 cohesin by separase, but also the separase-dependent removal of COH-3/4 cohesin and the role of separase-independent cohesin removal that occurs in late prophase.
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for future models, based on the new data presented.

claim: Different mechanisms trigger separase-independent removal of REC-8 from short arms and COH-3/4 from long arms.
source: Our finding that different mechanisms trigger separase-independent removal of REC-8 from short arms and COH-3/4 from long arms indicates that AIR-2 is not the sole factor to direct the stepwise separation of homologs and sisters.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that REC-8 removal requires AIR-2 while COH-3/4 removal does not.

claim: Removal of COH-3/4 from the long arm begins in diplotene, prior to AIR-2 accumulation at the midbivalent and coincident with the removal of synaptonemal complex from the long arm.
source: In contrast, COH-3/4 cohesin is removed from the long arm of wild-type animals beginning in diplotene, prior to AIR-2 accumulation at the midbivalent and coincident with the removal of SC from the long arm (Nabeshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B, and is consistent with prior literature on SC removal (Nabeshima et al., 2005).

claim: Both removal of COH-3/4 from the long arm and persistence of COH-3/4 at the short arm are independent of AIR-2 function.
source: Both removal of COH-3/4 from the long arm and persistence of COH-3/4 at the short arm are independent of AIR-2 function.
evidence: This is directly observed in immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Separase-independent partitioning of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins into reciprocal domains could explain why factors like Mei-S332/Shugoshin are not required in C. elegans.
source: The separase-independent partitioning of REC-8 and COH-3/4 cohesins into reciprocal domains could explain why factors like Mei-S332/Shugoshin, which protect centromeric cohesin from separase-mediated cleavage during anaphase I in monocentric organisms, are not required in C. elegans (de Carvalho et al., 2008; Severson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of separase-independent cohesin removal and prior knowledge that shugoshin is not required in C. elegans.

claim: Selective removal of REC-8 from the short arm may restrict co-orientation to the long arm.
source: In the second model, selective removal of REC-8 from the short arm does not determine the timing of separation for homologs vs sisters, but rather restricts co-orientation to the long arm.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors based on their data.

claim: Separase-dependent cleavage of COH-3/4 and any REC-8 remaining at the short arm would allow homologs to segregate toward opposite poles.
source: Once homologs have made proper attachments to microtubules and aligned on the metaphase plate, separase-dependent cleavage of COH-3/4 and any REC-8 remaining at the short arm would allow homologs to segregate toward opposite poles.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed by the authors based on their data.

claim: Plants and mammals require similar sets of meiotic kleisins as those in C. elegans.
source: Plants and mammals require similar sets of meiotic kleisins as those in C. elegans, demonstrating the widely conserved involvement of multiple kleisins in gametogenesis and highlighting the importance of understanding the mechanisms by which kleisins influence cohesin function.
evidence: This is established from prior literature showing the discovery of similar kleisins in plants and mammals (Herran et al., 2011; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011; Llano et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2012).

claim: In mice, synaptonemal complex proteins assemble between sister chromatids in Rec8 single mutants but not in Rad21L Rec8 double kleisin mutants.
source: For example, as in C. elegans (Figure 5A and Severson et al., 2009), SC proteins in mice assemble between sister chromatids in Rec8 single mutants but not in Rad21L Rec8 double kleisin mutants, demonstrating the involvement of multiple kleisins in SC assembly (Llano et al., 2012; Ishiguro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from Llano et al., 2012; Ishiguro et al., 2014.

claim: Partial cohesion persists in meiotic nuclei of mouse Rad21L Rec8 double mutants.
source: Moreover, the idea that factors other than known meiosis-specific cohesin complexes contribute to SCC during spermatogenesis is suggested by the persistence of partial cohesion in meiotic nuclei of mouse Rad21L Rec8 double mutants (Llano et al., 2012; Ishiguro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from Llano et al., 2012; Ishiguro et al., 2014.

claim: The mitotic kleisin RAD21 appears to associate with meiotic chromosomes of both wild-type and Rad21L Rec8 mutant mice.
source: The mitotic kleisin RAD21 appears to associate with meiotic chromosomes of both wild-type and Rad21L Rec8 mutants, suggesting that 'mitotic' cohesin might tether sisters during gametogenesis in mammals, as in worms (Prieto et al., 2002; Parra et al., 2004; Xu et al., 2004; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011; Llano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from multiple sources.

claim: High levels of REC8 were detected in premeiotic mouse nuclei.
source: High levels of REC8 were detected in premeiotic mouse nuclei, consistent with REC8 cohesin becoming cohesive during DNA replication (Eijpe et al., 2003; Ishiguro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from Eijpe et al., 2003; Ishiguro et al., 2014.

claim: RAD21L staining was faint in PCNA-positive premeiotic testicular cells but greatly increased on meiotic chromosomes during leptotene and zygotene in mice.
source: In contrast, RAD21L staining was faint in PCNA-positive premeiotic testicular cells but greatly increased on meiotic chromosomes during leptotene and zygotene (Herran et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011; Ishiguro et al., 2014), indicating that substantial amounts of RAD21L cohesin load after meiotic entry.
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from Herran et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011; Ishiguro et al., 2014.

claim: A Spo11 disruption exacerbated the sister chromatid cohesion defects of Rec8 knockout mice.
source: Indeed, a Spo11 disruption exacerbated the SCC defects of Rec8 knockout mice (Ishiguro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from Ishiguro et al., 2014.

claim: REC8 persists at high levels at centromeres and chromosome arms until anaphase I in mouse spermatocytes and oocytes.
source: Although REC8 persists at high levels at centromeres and chromosome arms until anaphase I in mouse spermatocytes and oocytes, RAD21L and RAD21 proteins progressively diminish in abundance during late prophase at chromosome arms of spermatocytes and at arms and centromeres of oocytes. (Prieto et al., 2002, 2004; Lee et al., 2003; Parra et al., 2004; Tachibana-Konwalski et al., 2010; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from multiple sources.

claim: RAD21L and RAD21 proteins progressively diminish in abundance during late prophase at chromosome arms of mouse spermatocytes and at arms and centromeres of oocytes.
source: Although REC8 persists at high levels at centromeres and chromosome arms until anaphase I in mouse spermatocytes and oocytes, RAD21L and RAD21 proteins progressively diminish in abundance during late prophase at chromosome arms of spermatocytes and at arms and centromeres of oocytes. (Prieto et al., 2002, 2004; Lee et al., 2003; Parra et al., 2004; Tachibana-Konwalski et al., 2010; Ishiguro et al., 2011; Lee and Hirano, 2011).
evidence: This is established from prior literature on mouse meiosis, cited from multiple sources.
